title: Element 10: Fire
learningObjectives: Describe the fire triangle and conditions required for fire
Classify fires and match them to the appropriate extinguishing agents
Outline fire risk assessment and means of escape requirements
Explain the causes and management of flammable substance hazards

content.text: Fire requires three elements to start and continue. Remove any one and the fire is extinguished.

rows: Anything that will burn — solid, liquid, gas
Remove fuel sources, store flammables safely, housekeeping
Enough energy to start and sustain combustion
Cool with water, remove ignition sources

content.text: The fire tetrahedron adds a fourth element — the chain reaction (free radicals that sustain combustion). Halon extinguishers (now banned) worked by interrupting this chain reaction. Dry powder also has some chain reaction interruption effect.

rows: Ordinary combustibles: wood, paper, textiles, plastics
Water, foam, dry powder, wet chemical
Flammable liquids: petrol, diesel, oil, paint
Flammable gases: LPG, natural gas, H2S
Dry powder — stop gas supply first

content.text: In any fire — first alert others, call emergency services, then only attempt to fight the fire if it is small, you have a clear escape route, you have the right extinguisher, and you have been trained. Never place yourself at risk.
A fire risk assessment identifies fuel sources, ignition sources, and oxygen sources; evaluates who is at risk; and determines fire prevention and protection measures.

items: Fuel sources — Identify and control all combustible materials; no unnecessary storage; separate flammables
Ignition sources — Hot work controls (PTW); no-smoking enforcement; electrical equipment maintenance; static electricity controls
Oxygen sources — Avoid oxygen enrichment; safe storage of compressed oxygen
Detection — Automatic fire detection (smoke, heat, flame detectors); regular testing
Suppression — Sprinkler systems, gaseous suppression for IT rooms/archives
Means of escape — Adequate fire exits; unobstructed; emergency lighting; evacuation plans
Fire fighting — Correct extinguisher types; trained fire wardens

content.text: Hydrocarbon fires (Class B and C) are the primary fire risk in Gulf O&G. Facilities use dedicated fire suppression systems: deluge systems for tank farms, dry powder for transformer areas, foam systems for crude oil storage. Hot work permits are the primary prevention control for ignition in high-risk areas. All HSE officers must know the facility's fire emergency response plan and mustering procedures.

The minimum concentration of a flammable gas or vapour in air that will ignite. Below the LEL the mixture is 'too lean' to burn. Atmospheric gas monitors alarm at 10% and 20% of LEL to give early warning.

The maximum concentration at which a gas/vapour will ignite. Above the UEL the mixture is 'too rich' to burn. However, as gas disperses, it will pass through the explosive range — do not assume a very high reading means 'safe'.

items: ATEX/IECEx zones: Zone 0 (continuous risk), Zone 1 (likely), Zone 2 (unlikely) — only Ex-rated equipment allowed
Earthing and bonding — Prevent static electricity buildup during transfer of flammables
Hot work controls — PTW; gas testing before and during hot work; fire watcher
Ventilation — Prevent accumulation of flammable vapours in enclosed spaces
